Results.ReviewText: Purchased 3 years ago at $500+ pricetag beacuse i thought itd be a quality product and it advertised a 10 year warranty on the box!  After 3 years the warming rack, grates, flavorizer bars and burner tubes are rusting through. I always clean and cover my grill. Called weber warranty support to take advantage of the warranty and the told me only the burner tubes and grates are covered. Disappointed they wont stand behind their product after they advertise the warranty.  Almost like printer ink i will need to spend another 20% of the original purchase to keep an under warranty grill working properly. Will look elsewhere went this grill is done.
Results.Title: Not sure it will last - too expensive for quality

Results.ReviewText: I like everything about my Weber except two things. First is the cast iron grates with the wide side up tend to collect food on the bottom side that can't be reached with a wire brush. Secondly, I wish the temperature controls were more responsive and labeled with set temperature. Example, if a recipe calls for direct heat 450 for 8 minutes turning once midway, when I open the lid to turn, I loose 100 degrees, and it takes the grill 2-3 minutes to regain that 100 degress which in this case is 30% of the remaining cooking time. I wish Weber had a diagram that showed the temperature with all 3 burners on, at all low and all midway.

Results.ReviewText: 've had Weber charcoal grills for over 40 years. I brought one which to this day is still in good condition from the East Coast to California. Unfortunately the smoke freaked out my neighbor who kept thinkin the neighborhood was on fire. So I got an inexpensive end-of-the-season gas grill. It lasted only one year before the company had to replace the burners and other components. Within the next year it rusted so badly the underneath tray was completely gone. I bought this Weber gas grill and have had it only a few weeks so nothing to compare. It seems better built except it is a little skewed if the ground is not 100% level. So Far I like it. It cooks well. It doesn't accept universal rotisseries which is a drag. I roast coffee and Im going to have to get a different rotisserie or make an adapter. Otherwise I'm pleased with it so far.

Results.ReviewText:
"You get what you pay for" and that's why we bought a Weber grill.  Great reviews and lots of family and friends who own Weber grills.  I cook for a living and enjoy using my grill year around.  We bought this Spirit E-310, 5 years ago along with the cover that goes with it.  Just 3 months ago I started to see paint peel away from the hood. Then two weeks ago the grill grates have started fall apart, and then holes were visible on flavorizer 
bars.  The last thing to go was the door falling off.  The pin at the bottom had base to hold onto.  I thought about replacing the bars and grates but when door fell off I was done.

46510001.Name: Spirit E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
46510001.Description:
Add flavor to the menu with a Spirit E-310. It’s the ideal grill for entertaining a small crowd or a perfect solution to any family meal. Place serving trays and spices on the side tables so that everything you need is where you are, when you need it. With features such as porcelain-enameled, cast-iron cooking grates that retain even heat, you’re guaranteed the best tasting food. It’s built to last with a cookbox that helps prevent rusting and peeling, and conveniently equipped with six tool hooks for easy accessibility of grilling tools. If that wasn’t enough, the low maintenance and easy-to-clean grease management system takes the hassle out of cooking.


• Durable, easy-to-clean porcelain-enamel cast iron grates.

• Porcelain-enameled finish helps prevent rusting and pealing.

• Six tool hooks for easy accessibility of grilling tools.

• Low maintenance and easy-to-clean grease management system.

• 424 square inches of main grilling space.


 This product requires assembly.
